title: AI made my game possible and I feel bad
author: PupperRobot
selftext:
Hi folks ,

Just curious if others feel this way too but ai basically made my game possible. Possibly in the sense that it helped me bring my own vision to life without too many place holder assets or thousands of dollars spent on graphic designers and modelers.

I initially wanted to go down the human route and got quotes from graphic designers and modelers for all of my needs and the total quote I got was over 20k... Obviously there was no way I was going to pay that. But I kept coding myself with placeholder free assets I got off of unity asset store. But this year AI tools got much better with everything so I got all of my visual assets done using ai. Obviously still spent some money but nowhere near the 20k it would've cost me and I was able to quickly prototype many different visual styles before settling on one all thanks for ai.

So why do I feel bad? Because my game and experience are proof that modelers and graphic designers are bound to lose their jobs. There is almost no need for them currently in game development. And within the next year it will be even worse for them. Does anyone feel this way also?

comments.author: Any-Gap-933
comments.body: I'm glad you realized it, but the same that has happened in history enough times with each human technological advance and humans are still here with different jobs.

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body: You feel bad because a small but very vocal group is trying to make the use of AI immoral

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: I don't think it's immoral at all. And those people can't make me feel that way. But I can observe the obvious outcome and feel bad still

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
Anything that create something on internet for public, will guarantee to meet some kind of hate.

The same group that hate ai today, will hate something else when they have new trend.

If random comment on internet gets you, than i suggest find other profesion.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: I didn't get any comments haha this is just how I felt after using ai instead of paying humans.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Modelers and graphic designers are only loosing their job if they don’t keep keep up and won’t use AI in the process because some other modeler or graphic designer will use it. Every professional modeler is better than us and could improve AI generated Models in a way we couldn’t

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: But I feel like even if they do use AI for their work there is no need for them. Especially for modelers. There will come a time where any reference image will be turned into a perfect game ready 3D asset. I know tripo and meshy exist now and they'll only get better moving forward. Maybe graphic designers will have better luck because I'm sure there will some need for niche art ai may or may not be able to ever produce but they're also at large risk.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: It's true.  It isn't a black and white choice between pro and anti AI.  Fact is people will lose their jobs and that's just part of technology advancing.  It's ok to feel bad about it and embrace the new tech as well.  In fact that's kinda the most honest approach, because you're not gonna hold back the tide.

replies.body:

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body:
Don't feel bad, every new generation of technology, throughout human history has led to obsolete artisans and craftsmen. If you aren't learning new skills, you are waiting to become extinct. Using AI is the newest, and maybe one of the most valuable skills in existence now. 

Making games with AI is not easy to do well. You can make some derivative copy with enough brute force, but to use these powerful tools and techniques wisely and with good taste... that's actually a huge differentiator.

TLDR; you shouldn't feel guilty, it's astounding just how good the technology is becoming. It is having a cohesive and compelling dream, and then harnessing discipline and willpower that is the hard part now.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: technological innovation allows everyone to level up the amount of work they're capable of doing. The term "computers" came from a job where people in a room were tasked with performing calculations that were handed down to them. Traditional 2D animation had entire ink and paint departments shut down with the advent of automatic digital ink and paint computer software, in-betweening was a profession, as was the camera crew needed to shoot and digitize each frame for pencil tests. No 2D animator would want to go back to the old way of 2D animation since they can now make a whole animated short/film on their own computer.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: Was just talking to my boss the other day about what happened to the architecture and engineering world when CAD came out.  Rough!  But also awesome.  And early CAD was just as janky as early AI... There were plenty of non-believers until it became so convenient it was practically required.

comments.author: JeeCharns
comments.body:
It’s a tough cookie. I think you just have to embrace it, in 10-20 years I hypothesise nobody will be asking this question or perceiving any moral dilemma.

When you buy clothes, do you feel bad because it was made by a machine and not by hand? 

No, but when the Industrial Revolution happened people burnt down looms in the north of England because weavers lost their jobs. (You may feel bad if it was made in a sweatshop but that’s a different moral issue).

I think there will always be a place for hand crafted visuals especially in big budget productions and studios. Just like there is still a place for hand made clothes. It’s just the barrier to entry has collapsed for indie devs.

comments.author: StarMonkeyGames
comments.body:
Here's the thing. We're all being automated out. The skills we all trained and thought were marketable are losing their value. We are all in the same boat. Don't feel bad. Figure out how to stay afloat first, then worry about others. 

I'm not mad at you for using AI to program. And I'm not mad at people for using Art to generate assets. These tools are out. 

Like no one is stopping artists from scaling up their work. They could be making video games and showing off their art through more complex mediums. 

Anyway. Be smart. Use what's available or get left behind. 

And if you do feel bad later. Replacing all of the AI generated stuff is probably a solid marketing idea in the future. But like who knows. 

Maybe you charge less for the game. Who knows? You won't know until you try and get there.

Anyway, don't listen to Reddit. It's is an echochamber filled like young college kids who never had a professional job. Reddit is not any more wise than Twitter or whatever stupid social media platform.  
  
Because in the real world. AI is already the default. All the software you use from all the giants are done with AI. This is like a top down command from corporate.

comments.author: MacIntoic
comments.body: Why do you think game development needs you more than it needs modellers and graphic designers? And what makes you think your game has any commercial value when anyone can create it with almost no cost and no technical ability?

replies.author: NotagirlDK
replies.body: This. I would love to have the money to pay artists, they're better in all ways still, messy outputs are kind of grim, and super limited.

comments.author: DoctaRoboto
comments.body:
People will either adapt or lose their jobs; this has always happened. My mother was a librarian and never used a computer in her life before; she only used notebooks and folders until the library got "modernized". She really struggled for some months and survived.

AI will also help clean the artist community of untalented and abusive people. Just this week I saw two $600 "man-made" game capsules that looked like shit. As an artist myself (even if I am a painter and I don't design capsules), I would feel ashamed of doing such a crappy, sloppy job.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: I think it's overly ambitious to think AI is gonna clean anything.  For every untalented and or abusive mofo it displaces, it'll bring in another whose whole thing is knowing about AI.  But otherwise I agree

comments.author: Short_Stable2397
comments.body:
I think the core fallacy with your reasoning is that, with or without AI, you never had the money to pay the artists anyway. So the artists, with or without AI, never lost your custom.

If you made money with AI, you'd probably spend that on real artists. That is potential extra money they could earn in the future due to AI.

How do you like them apples, or am I coping too hard?

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: ... You are actually making sense here. I could've never hired them in the first place 😁
